changes.title: RISE Changes: a list starts under its title, and the composer is told each kit slot's budget
SVC-002 records the density finding, #701 and its dry run
RISE Changes: a density floor, list and compare figures, density in the score, and supersede
Generate experimental GitHits SBOMs for published releases
Review dependency changes with cached license and vulnerability policy
Enable pinned docs search and OSS example grounding for agents
SVC-002 records the eye's exemption from the hold limit and its dry run
RISE Changes: RISE's eye, the room at rest, is exempt from the hold limit
SVC-002 records the opening-and-close change and its dry run
RISE Changes: engines are named only as the opening and the close
Route GitHits agent lookups through private usage accounting
SVC-002 records the held-pictures fix and its dry run
A digest's picture ends where its beats move on, and the reading returns to RISE's eye; the page says plainly why a change was left out
SVC-002 records the alignment fix's merge and a first-pass dry run
A digest's picture sits on the beat that speaks of it, shows what words cannot, and an unspoken change is left out instead of repaired
SVC-002 records the figure kit's merge and its dry run
RISE draws its own figures with the Figure Kit: bars, flows, columns and stacks whose labels cannot collide
The connector logs one count of each admitted Current's figure problems and picture cadence, and answers exactly as before
RISE Changes holds every picture's labels and every beat's words to mechanical checks, and scores each run's first pass
SVC-002 records the third dry run and the real digest with pictures, /changes/2026-10-15

beats.say: This week RISE Changes learned to draw its own figures, and to check its own work.
RISE now draws figures itself, from data. There are four kinds: bars, flows, columns and stacks.
Every label is measured before it is drawn. A label that does not fit is refused, never shrunk, so labels cannot collide.
Each beat of a digest also carries the numbers of the pull requests it speaks about. The sources are now written from those numbers.
Two more kinds arrived later in the week: a list, and a compare for a before and after. A rule or a process change now has a figure that fits it.
A picture must now sit on the beat that speaks of it. Pictures that show nothing the words do not, like sparse columns, are refused.
A change that no beat speaks of is no longer repaired into the reading. It is left out, and the page says so.

A picture also ends where its beats move on, and the reading returns to RISE's eye. The page now gives plain reasons for a change left out: minor, skipped by the router, records only, over the 24-change limit, or not spoken of.
The published digest showed only 2 pictures in 19 beats. So there is now a density floor: no more than two speaking beats in a row without a picture, and every major change gets one.
The score now records density too, so a picture that is let go counts against the run.
A published period can also be superseded. The re-run takes the next id, the old entry links to the new reading, and the old file is never touched.
Figure labels are now held to mechanical checks. Each failure seen in a real run became a check that answers with a sentence the model can repair from.
A browser then draws each admitted figure at phone size and desktop size, and measures every label. A fault goes back to the illustrator once.
The composer's words are checked for process talk. Each run is scored on its first pass, and the page shows the score.

On the infrastructure side, pull requests now get a dependency review. A critical advisory in a changed dependency blocks. License drift warns. Without credentials, it warns that coverage was skipped.
Published releases also gain an experimental software bill of materials, attached with digests of its source and output.
No real export has been generated yet, and the live credentials are unverified.
